title: The Castle of Otranto — Before Philosophy Got Polite #Shorts
description:
Nothing in The Castle of Otranto was built for you — it was built for reproduction. The Castle of Otranto is a novel written by the British Whig politician and historian and Horace Walpole. First published in 1764, it is generally regarded as the first Gothic novel.

The genes do not care about The Castle of Otranto; they care about copies. The Catholic element was a necessary facet of the "template of terror" that Walpole meant to invoke. The allusion to Hamlet's experience with the Ghost is meant not only as a "template of terror," but also to make readers feel as if they are watching the play itself, and Walpole does this on three occasions.

scenes.narration: Nothing in The Castle of Otranto was built for you — it was built for reproduction. The Castle
of Otranto is a novel written by the British Whig politician and historian and Horace Walpole. First published
in 1764, it is generally regarded as the first Gothic novel. The psychology underneath The Castle of Otranto
is simpler and older than the story on top. In the second edition, Walpole applied the word 'Gothic'
to the novel in the subtitle – A Gothic Story. Set in a haunted castle, the novel merged
medievalism and terror in a style that has endured ever since. Behind The Castle of Otranto sits an
animal brain negotiating with a story it
